claims.text: The baseline is a soft magnetic HEA containing a high volume fraction of coherent, ordered nanoprecipitates.
Nanoprecipitates smaller than the magnetic domain-wall thickness interact minimally with domain walls.
High precipitate–matrix coherency produces negligible distortion fields and modest domain-wall pinning.
Composition tailoring and aging can grow the nanoprecipitates to a size comparable to or larger than the domain-wall thickness.
The proposed heat treatment will decrease precipitate coherency with the matrix.
Controlled coarsening can occur without significantly altering the overall phase composition.
Precipitates begin to pin domain walls effectively when their size reaches a critical value comparable to the domain-wall thickness.
Larger, partially incoherent nanoprecipitates are stronger domain-wall pinning centers than small, coherent nanoprecipitates.
Loss of full coherency increases local strain fields and interfacial disturbances.
Local strain fields and interfacial disturbances hinder magnetic domain-wall motion.
Stronger domain-wall pinning requires a higher applied field to reverse magnetization and therefore increases coercivity.
An HEA with larger, less coherent precipitates will have a higher coercive field than the matched baseline with small, coherent precipitates.
The coercivity enhancement requires the precipitates to reach or exceed a size comparable to the domain-wall thickness.
The coercivity enhancement requires the structural integrity of the matrix to remain intact.
Excessively large precipitates or excessive inhomogeneity can undermine magnetic exchange coupling and prevent the desired coercivity increase.
Failure of the coarsened, less coherent condition to produce a statistically significant coercivity increase relative to the control would falsify the hypothesis.
